tools.name: add_code_connect_map

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. componentName.description: The name of the component to map to in the source code

label.description: The framework or language label for this Code Connect mapping. Valid values: React, Web Components, Vue, Svelte, Storybook, Javascript, Swift, Swift UIKit, Objective-C UIKit, SwiftUI, Compose, Java, Kotlin, Android XML Layout, Flutter, Markdown

templateDataJson.description: JSON string of template metadata. May include isParserless (boolean), imports, nestable, props fields. If omitted when template is provided, defaults to {}.

tools.name: create_generative_plugin

If it is not installed, read skill://figma/figma-generative-plugins/SKILL.md with resources/read or get_figma_skill. Use this for requests to build, create, upload, or publish a “Figma plugin,” “generative plugin,” or “custom tool.” It creates a generative plugin in the account library; it does not install an existing Figma Community plugin. Creates a new generative plugin in the authenticated user's account library and returns its id. The plugin starts as a working scaffold — a runnable starter that draws a square — so it is a structural starting point, not a finished plugin: follow this call with the update tool to replace the scaffold's source with the behavior the user asked for. planKey names the plan that will own the plugin; take it from the plans list returned by whoami.

name.description: Display name for the new resource.

planKey.description: The team or organization key (e.g. "team::1234567890" or "organization::1234567890"). Use the `key` field verbatim from one of the user's plans. If the user has more than one plan, ask which one to use before calling.

tools.name: create_new_file
tools.description: Create a new blank Figma file. IMPORTANT: You MUST load the /figma-create-new-file skill BEFORE every call to this tool, if it exists. NEVER call this tool without loading that skill first if it exists. By default the file is placed in the authenticated user's drafts folder; If specified it can be placed inside a project. Use this tool when you need a new file to work with before calling use_figma. Returns the new file key and URL. Always include all three required arguments: fileName, planKey, and editorType. For editorType, use "design", "figjam", or "slides". If the user already provided a planKey, use it directly. Otherwise, call the whoami tool first to get the list of plans. If the user has one plan, use its "key" field. If multiple, ask the user which team or organization to use. Optionally accepts a projectId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/files/project/:projectId, https://figma.com/files/:orgId/project/:projectId, or https://figma.com/files/team/:teamId/project/:projectId then use the :projectId as the projectId.

fileName.description: The name for the new Figma file.

planKey.description: The team or organization key (e.g. "team::1234567890" or "organization::1234567890"). Use the `key` field verbatim from one of the user's plans. If the user has more than one plan, ask which one to use before calling.

editorType.description: The type of Figma file to create. "design" creates a Figma design file. "figjam" creates a FigJam whiteboard file. "slides" creates a Figma Slides presentation file. "figmake" creates an empty Figma Make file and returns its make_node_id; follow it with send_code_to_figma to import a project or send_prompt to generate an app, when those tools are available.

projectId.description: The id of the project (folder) in Figma. If the URL is provided, extract the project id from the URL. Common URL formats include https://figma.com/files/project/:projectId, https://figma.com/files/:orgId/project/:projectId, and https://figma.com/files/team/:teamId/project/:projectId. The extracted projectId would be `:projectId`.

Set kind to effect for a shader that transforms the layer beneath it, or fill for a shader that generates its own pixels. The resource starts as a working scaffold, so follow this call with the update tool to replace the scaffold's source with the shader the user asked for. planKey names the plan that will own the shader; take it from the plans list returned by whoami.

name.description: Display name for the new resource.

description.description: One-line description of what the resource does.

planKey.description: The team or organization key (e.g. "team::1234567890" or "organization::1234567890"). Use the `key` field verbatim from one of the user's plans. If the user has more than one plan, ask which one to use before calling.

kind.description: The shader kind: effect transforms the layer beneath it; fill generates its own pixels.

tools.name: download_assets
tools.description: Download assets from a Figma file for a single node: an exported render, the original source images, and SVGs of the vector layers. The response contains: (1) `export` — an exported image of the whole node; (2) `rawImages` — original uploaded source images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP) found as fills anywhere in the node subtree (capped at 20); and (3) `svgAssets` — SVGs for the vector layers in the subtree that are best represented as SVG (icons, logos, simple illustrations), the same set get_design_context surfaces (capped at 20). Each raw image carries a `format` field with its actual image format (e.g. "png", "jpeg", "gif", "webp") so you can save it with the correct file extension; if the format cannot be determined it is reported as "original". Each `svgAssets` entry has format "svg". Call this tool for asset URLs get_design_context has not already provided: the `export` render of the whole node, a specific format or scale, or assets for a node you have not requested design context for. Export precedence: when you pass defaultFormat and/or defaultScale, those override the export settings configured on the node in Figma. When you omit them, the node-configured export settings are used if present, otherwise png at scale 1. Pass defaultFormat or defaultScale only when the user explicitly asks for a specific format, size, or resolution. For cross-file image transfer, use the raw image URLs with upload_assets. URLs are temporary — download promptly. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), Figma Slides (`/slides/`), and FigJam boards (`/board/`). Does NOT work on Figma Make files (`/make/`).

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

defaultFormat.description: Export format. When you provide this, it overrides any export settings configured on the node in Figma. When you omit it, the node-configured export format is used if present, otherwise png. Set this only when the user asks for a specific format.

defaultScale.description: Export scale (resolution multiplier). When you provide this, it overrides any export settings configured on the node in Figma. When you omit it, the node-configured export scale is used if present, otherwise 1. Set this only when the user asks for a specific size or resolution.

tools.name: export_video
tools.description: Export a Figma timeline node as an MP4 video. This tool only produces MP4 — GIF and animated SVG export are not supported yet. Renders the timeline server-side and returns a presigned download URL. The file stays available for `ttlSeconds` (defaults to 1 hour, clamped server-side to [30s, 7d]); use `availableUntil` in the response to know when it is deleted. Some renders finish in seconds, others take minutes; if the render hasn't finished within the handler budget, the response includes a `jobId` and `status: "processing"` — re-invoke `export_video` with `{ fileKey, jobId }` after 10–15s to poll. Required: `fileKey` and either `nodeId` (to start a new export) or `jobId` (to poll). The `nodeId` must be the top-level frame that owns the timeline — in a design file a frame placed directly on the page or in a section, and in Slides the slide itself (not a layer inside it) — not a nested layer or sub-clip. If you animated a descendant, pass its containing top-level frame (the slide, in Slides); if `get_motion_context` returns a `timelineCohorts` entry, its `rootNodeId` is that frame. Use the `quality` field ("low"/"medium"/"high") to control output size.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

nodeId.description: The timeline node to export. Required when starting a new export. Provide nodeId OR jobId, never both — the call is rejected if both are set. Must be the top-level frame that owns the timeline — in a design file a frame placed directly on the page or in a section, and in Slides the slide itself (not a layer inside it) — not a nested layer or sub-clip. If you animated a descendant, pass its containing top-level frame (the slide, in Slides); if get_motion_context returns a `timelineCohorts` entry, its `rootNodeId` is that frame.

fps.description: Frames per second for the rendered MP4 (5-60). Optional; the server picks a default.

quality.description: Render quality preset. Higher quality means a larger file. Optional; the server picks a default.

constraint.description: Output-size constraint. SCALE multiplies the node's natural size (value is the multiplier, e.g. 2 = 2x); WIDTH / HEIGHT pin that dimension to an absolute pixel count and scale the other to preserve aspect ratio. Optional; omit to render at the node's natural size (1x). Clamped server-side to a max 10x scale / 4096px per dimension. Ignored when polling with jobId.

ttlSeconds.description: How long (in seconds) the rendered MP4 is retained on the server. Each poll reissues a fresh presigned download URL; once this window elapses the file is deleted and the job is no longer reachable. Clamped server-side to [30, 7d].

jobId.description: Returned from a previous call when the export was still rendering. Pass this to poll. Provide nodeId OR jobId, never both — the call is rejected if both are set. When polling, fps/quality/ttlSeconds are ignored (they were fixed when the job was created).

tools.name: generate_diagram
tools.description: Create a flowchart, decision tree, gantt chart, sequence diagram, state diagram, or entity relationship diagram in FigJam, using Mermaid.js. Generated diagrams should be simple, unless a user asks for details. This tool also does not support generating Figma designs, class diagrams, timelines, venn diagrams, or other Mermaid.js diagram types. This tool also does not support font changes, or moving individual shapes around -- if a user asks for those changes to an existing diagram, encourage them to open the diagram in Figma. If the tool is unable to complete the user's task, reference the error that is passed back. Do not use the create_new_file tool prior to creating a diagram using this tool; generate_diagram creates its own files.

name.description: A human-readable title for the diagram. Keep it short, but descriptive.

mermaidSyntax.description:
Mermaid.js code for the diagram. Keep diagrams simple, unless the user has detailed requirements. Only the following diagram types are supported: graph, flowchart, sequenceDiagram, stateDiagram, stateDiagram-v2, gantt, and erDiagram. Make sure to use correct Mermaid.js syntax. For graph, flowchart, or entity relationship diagrams, use LR direction by default and put all shape and edge text in quotes (eg. ["Text"], -->|"Edge Text"|, --"Edge Text"-->). Do not use emojis in the Mermaid.js code. Do not use 
 to represent new lines. Feel free to use the full range of shapes and connectors that Mermaid.js syntax offers. For graph and flowchart diagrams only, you can use color styling--but do so sparingly unless the user asks for it. In gantt charts, do not use color styling. In sequence diagrams, do not use notes. Do not use the word "end" in classNames.

userIntent.description: A description of what the user is trying to accomplish with this tool call. Important: Do not add extraneous information other than what the user provides.

planKey.description: The team or organization key (e.g. "team::1234567890" or "organization::1234567890"). Use the `key` field verbatim from one of the user's plans. If the user has more than one plan, ask which one to use before calling.

savePlanKey.description: Optional. Indicates whether to use the same plan for future generations. Do not provide this parameter unless the user specifically requests it, and a planKey is also provided.

useArchitectureLayoutCode.description: Optional. To generate a diagram using the software architecture layout, pass the code from the architecture-diagram-instructions resource. Omit this parameter for standard diagrams.

fileKey.description: Optional. The key of an existing FigJam file to add the diagram to. Extract from a Figma URL like figma.com/board/{fileKey}/... When provided, the diagram is placed directly in this file instead of creating a new one. The user must have edit access to the file.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate a raster image from a text prompt using state-of-the-art image models. Width and height guide the aspect ratio; the model chooses a supported output size, so the image pixel dimensions may differ from the requested values. The tool returns a URL serving the raw image bytes of a PNG or JPEG image. IMPORTANT: The URL expires after 7 days. The user MUST download the image before the URL expires to keep a copy. **This is a paid feature — each call consumes Figma AI credits against the user's plan (different models have different per-call costs).** Alternatively, provide fileKey instead of planKey to generate and place the image directly in an editable Design, FigJam, or Slides file. If no editable file exists, call create_new_file first. File mode checks AI permissions and credits against the destination file. Omit nodeId to create a new image-filled frame, or provide nodeId to replace an existing image fill without resizing it. File mode returns fileKey, nodeId, model, width, and height for download_assets, without a temporary URL. Always provide exactly one of planKey (URL mode) or fileKey (placement mode); nodeId is only valid in file mode.

prompt.description: Text description of the image to generate.

model.description: Image model to use. One of: gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image, gpt-image-2.5-sunburst, gemini-3.1-flash-image. Defaults to gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image.

width.description: Requested width in pixels. Together with height, selects the closest supported aspect ratio; actual image width may differ. Default: 1024; max: 2048.

height.description: Requested height in pixels. Together with width, selects the closest supported aspect ratio; actual image height may differ. Default: 1024; max: 2048.

fileKey.description: Destination file for image placement. Provide either fileKey or planKey, never both.

nodeId.description: Existing node whose image fill should be replaced without resizing it. Omit to create a new frame.

planKey.description: Deprecated. Prefer fileKey to place the generated image in a file. Use planKey only for legacy temporary-URL generation, and never provide it together with fileKey.

tools.name: get_design_context
tools.description: Get design context for a Figma node — the primary tool for design-to-code workflows. Returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual metadata that must be adapted to the target project. IMPORTANT: You MUST load figma-design-to-code guidance BEFORE calling this tool. Prefer the /figma-design-to-code skill if available; otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md MCP resource. NEVER call this tool without loading that guidance first — skipping it produces code that ignores the target project's existing components, design tokens, and conventions. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. If a URL is provided, extract the node id and file key from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2` and the fileKey would be `:fileKey`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName then use the makeFileKey to identify the Figma Make file. Only for Figma Make files (URLs containing `/make/`), and only when calling get_design_context, assume the nodeId is `0:1`. The response will contain a code string and a JSON of download URLs for the assets referenced in the code. It will also include a screenshot of the node for context by default.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

clientLanguages.description: A comma separated list of programming languages used by the client in the current context in string form, e.g. `javascript`, `html,css,typescript`, etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which languages are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess.

clientFrameworks.description: A comma separated list of frameworks used by the client in the current context, e.g. `react`, `vue`, `django` etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which frameworks are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess

forceCode.description: Whether code should always be returned, instead of returning just metadata if the output size is too large. Only set this when the user directly requests to force the code.

disableCodeConnect.description: Whether Code Connect should be used to get the design context. Only set this when the user directly requests to disable Code Connect.

skillNames.description: A comma-separated list of Figma skill names being followed, if any (e.g. "figma-design-to-code", "figma-design-to-code,figma-code-connect"). Only pass this when explicitly instructed to by skill documentation. Used for logging purposes. If the skill was loaded via a skill-content MCP resource, prefix the skill name with "resource:". (e.g. "resource:figma-design-to-code", "resource:figma-design-to-code,resource:figma-code-connect")

excludeScreenshot.description: Whether to exclude the screenshot of the design from the response. IMPORTANT: it is not recommended to exclude screenshots. Only set this to true if the user has explicitly requested it or you are trying to preserve context.

tools.name: get_figjam

Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. IMPORTANT: This tool only works for FigJam files (URL path `/board/`), not other Figma files.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the FigJam board, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". If a URL is provided, extract the node id from the FigJam board URL, e.g. for https://figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2 the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`. A `/design/...` URL is NOT a FigJam file — do not call this tool with a design fileKey.

includeImagesOfNodes.description: Whether to include images of nodes in the response

tools.name: get_figma_skill
tools.description: Read a single Figma skill resource (the skill index, a SKILL.md, or a skill reference file) by its skill:// URI and return its text content. You MUST ONLY use skill:// URIs. You MUST NOT use this for any other resource (docs, Make source, files, node data, etc.). Discover URIs from the server instructions or by reading the skill index at "skill://index.json". A SKILL.md links to its reference files with relative paths (e.g. references/foo.md); read those as skill://figma/<skill-name>/references/<path>. To read several resources (for example a skill plus its reference files), call this tool once per URI.

uri.description: The skill resource URI to read: the skill index ("skill://index.json"), a SKILL.md ("skill://figma/<skill-name>/SKILL.md"), or a reference file ("skill://figma/<skill-name>/references/<path>"). Only skill:// URIs are supported — discover them in the server instructions or the skill://index.json index. Returns the resource text content.

tools.name: get_generative_plugin
tools.description: Reads a generative plugin from the account library by id (from list_generative_plugins), returning its name, description, owner, version, and a manifest of its source files as { filename, bytes, uri }. Owner is the authenticated user's email when they own the plugin, or a public publisher handle otherwise. Read each file's contents from its uri as an MCP resource (contents are not inlined here). Only set includeSource to true to add source to each file when the MCP client cannot read MCP resources. Pass an optional version (commit SHA) to read a specific build; defaults to the latest.

id.description: The id of the resource to read, taken from the matching list tool.

version.description: Optional 40-character commit SHA. Defaults to the latest built version.

includeSource.description: Include each file's source directly in the tool result, up to 100 files and 1,000,000 cumulative bytes. The result reports which limit caused truncation. Leave this false unless the MCP client cannot read MCP resources.

tools.name: get_libraries
tools.description: Get the design libraries associated with a Figma file. Returns two lists: (1) libraries currently added to the file (subscribed), and (2) libraries available to add (community UI kits and organization libraries). Each library includes its name, library key, description, and source type. The organization libraries portion of libraries_available_to_add is paginated — when the response includes a libraries_available_to_add_next_offset value, pass it back via the offset parameter to fetch the next page. Use the library keys from the response to scope searches with search_design_system by passing them as includeLibraryKeys.

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). The nodeId parameter is optional: when omitted, the tool returns a list of the top-level pages (guid + name) in the document instead of an XML dump — use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into. When the user has a current selection relevant to the request, the response is prepended with a "Currently selected nodes:" block listing the selection by guid and name, so you can tell whether it matches the queried nodeId. If the URL includes `node-id`, extract it and pass it as nodeId; for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, do not set nodeId; omit the field so the tool lists top-level pages. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

tools.name: get_screenshot
tools.description: Generate a screenshot for a given node or the currently selected node in the Figma desktop app. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). The optional `maxDimension` parameter (positive integer, max 65536, default 1024) caps the longer edge of the rendered PNG in pixels — increase it when you need to inspect fine detail, decrease it for thumbnails or to save context. The JSON metadata entry in the response includes both `width`/`height` (the rendered PNG size) and `original_width`/`original_height` (the node's natural canvas size before any clamping), so callers can decide whether to re-request at a higher `maxDimension`. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. nodeId parameter is REQUIRED. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. fileKey parameter is REQUIRED. If a URL is provided, extract the file key and node id from the URL. For example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/pqrs/ExampleFile?node-id=1-2 the extracted fileKey would be `pqrs` and the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). By default this tool returns a short-lived URL to the screenshot plus curl instructions for downloading the PNG — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding the image inline. The `enableBase64Response` parameter defaults to `false`. Only set `enableBase64Response: true` when the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests); when set, an inline base64 image entry is appended to the response in addition to the URL and curl instructions. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

contentsOnly.description: When true, renders the node in isolation — floating/overlapping content (e.g. connectors parented to the page that visually sit above a section) is excluded. Defaults to false so screenshots match what the user sees on the canvas. Only set to true if the caller specifically needs the isolated render.

enableBase64Response.description: When true, the response also includes the screenshot inline as a base64-encoded image entry, in addition to the short-lived URL and curl instructions. Defaults to false. Set to true ONLY if the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests)

maxDimension.description: Optional. Maximum pixel size of the longer edge of the rendered screenshot — the server scales the node so that max(width, height) ≤ maxDimension while preserving aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024. Must be a positive integer; values above 65536 are rejected. Increase when the agent will visually inspect fine detail; decrease for thumbnails or to save context.

tools.name: list_file_components_for_code_connect
tools.description: List every component and component set PUBLISHED to a Figma file's library, with the cross-component dependency graph needed to plan Code Connect in bulk. Only published components are returned (unpublished/local-only components are omitted). Returns one entry per component with its properties (exhaustive variant options, defaults, SLOT descriptions), page and asset/library membership, instance count, and direct dependencies (each flagged internal vs. external). Child instances and text layers include selector paths, property references, visibility, and owning component-set variants. Instance records include resolved master identity and property definitions; text records include sample content from the placed layer. Equivalent records across variants are combined with one sample nodeId. Instance-swap children are included but are not dependency edges. Unlike get_context_for_code_connect — which returns the deep descendant tree for one known component — this returns the flat whole-file graph for dependency-ordered, batched template generation. Takes only a file key (no node id). Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. If a URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName, the extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

tools.name: list_file_shaders
tools.description: Lists the shader effects and shader fills used in a Figma file. Returns each shader as { id, name, description, type, version, published, truncated, files }, where type is "effect" (post-effect that samples an input raster) or "fill" (generates pixels directly), published indicates whether the shader is a published library version, and files is a manifest of its authored source files as { filename, uri }. When truncated is true, the manifest hit its 10,000-file safety cap and is not exhaustive. The top-level truncated field is true when a referenced shader could not be returned, including when the file references more than the 100 returned shaders. Read each file's contents from its uri as an MCP resource (contents are not inlined here). Requires view access to the file. Use this to inspect shaders in a file you can open, including ones you do not own. Source reads are pinned to the exact shader version referenced by the file.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

tools.name: send_code_to_figma
tools.description: Import a local project into Figma Code. Requires edit access to a standalone Code or Design file. Does not create native Design shapes. Before choosing or creating a destination file, load figma-code-workflows. Target: standalone Code uses its empty main layer, including a starter. Design creates a new layer on pageId (default: first page). For populated Make, create a blank file. Same-target repair requires returned repairFrom: keep fileKey, seedId and makeNodeId; upload the corrected complete project. Changed or successful imports cannot be replaced. Legacy layers are unsupported. Start with the destination, omitting upload, to request instructions. Follow the returned source-configuration and archive guidance; local dependency installation, dev servers, HTTP checks and builds are not required. Static HTML/CSS/JS needs no setup scripts. Create the archive at nextStep.localArchivePath, then run nextStep.uploadCommand. Only after upload succeeds, call send_code_to_figma with nextStep.thenCall.arguments unchanged within one hour. upload.archivePath is a Figma storage path, never a local path. Keep makeNodeId/createLayer and any pageId/repairFrom unchanged. Do not resume failed uploads or retry ambiguous failures. Returns importReceipt, fileUrl, fileKey and nodeId. needs_setup preserves valid source with setupError; follow returned recovery instructions. Unsafe archives/access failures still fail. For import_pending, follow the continuation. Imported does not verify installation, preview or publishing. Open the file to start preview.

fileKey.description: The file key from a Figma Code /make/<fileKey> or Design /design/<fileKey> URL.

pageId.description: The destination page for a new code layer in a Design file. Defaults to the first page. Omit for a standalone file.

repairFrom.description: Use only to repair an unchanged needs_setup import in the same file and code layer.

upload.description: Uploaded-archive reference. Omit to request upload instructions. Only after a successful upload, copy nextStep.thenCall.arguments.upload unchanged to continue the import. Keep the returned repairFrom when repairing.

tools.name: upload_assets
tools.description: Upload assets (images and SVGs) into a Figma file. Call with a "count" to get that many single-use upload URLs. POST raw asset bytes to each URL with the correct Content-Type header (e.g. image/png, image/jpeg, image/svg+xml). Each upload URL handles storage, BlobStore commit, and canvas placement automatically. Use nodeIds to set raster images as fills on corresponding existing nodes; its order matches the returned upload URLs. Returned upload entries include targetNodeId when a target was provided. Without a target node, creates new frames with image fills on currentPageId when provided, otherwise on the current page. SVGs (image/svg+xml) are imported as editable vector node trees on that page; nodeIds and scaleMode do not apply to SVGs. Supports PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, and SVG. Max 10MB per asset. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). Request at most 60 upload URLs per call, then POST to every returned URL before calling upload_assets again. Repeat until all assets have been uploaded.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

currentPageId.description: The GUID of the page to target. Always pass this when available. Use the page the user is currently viewing unless the request explicitly refers to a different page.

count.description: Number of assets to upload. Returns that many single-use upload URLs. POST raw asset bytes to each URL with the correct Content-Type header (e.g. image/png, image/jpeg); the URLs can be POSTed in parallel. By default, each upload URL handles storage, BlobStore commit, and canvas placement automatically.

batchCommit.description: Optional. Set to true only if you can call the returned commitUrl exactly once after all uploads complete. When enabled server-side, this commits and places all assets in one file operation. If omitted, each upload URL commits and places its asset automatically.

nodeId.description: Deprecated: use nodeIds instead. If provided, sets the uploaded raster image as a fill on this existing node. Can only be used when count is 1. Ignored for SVGs, which are imported as vector node trees.

nodeIds.description: Optional target node IDs, one per upload URL in the same order. Each uploaded raster image is set as a fill on its corresponding existing node. The array length must equal count. Cannot be combined with nodeId. Ignored for SVGs, which are imported as vector node trees.

items.description: Existing target node ID for the corresponding upload URL, in the format "123:456".

scaleMode.description: How a raster image fills the node. Default: FILL. Ignored for SVGs.

tools.name: use_figma
tools.description: Create, edit, generate, or sync any design in Figma — UIs, screens, mockups, components, frames, variables, styles, text, images, layouts, and design systems. This general-purpose tool writes to Figma with JavaScript via the Figma Plugin API. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, load figma-use guidance — prefer the /figma-use skill if available, otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md MCP resource if available. Skipping this causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Use this tool when the user wants to: - Create or generate a Figma design, screen, UI, or mockup from scratch, intent, or code - Update, edit, or sync an existing Figma design - Generate or sync Figma designs from source code - Set up or modify design tokens, variables, or styles - Build or extend a design system or component/variant library - Fix layout, spacing, auto-layout, or fill/hug issues - Add component descriptions, annotations and Code Connect metadata to nodes - Review or fix accessibility, contrast, typography, or visual polish - Inspect or query node properties programmatically CHOOSING BETWEEN use_figma AND generate_figma_design: - Default to use_figma for all write operations - Exception: generate_figma_design ONLY to capture a web app page/view for the first time. For web apps, run both in parallel — generate_figma_design captures a pixel-perfect screenshot, use_figma builds from imported design system components and refines against the screenshot - Non-web (iOS, Android, generic UI) and from-scratch designs: use_figma only - Updating/syncing a Figma page already captured: use_figma — even if source code changed GOTCHAS - For the font "Inter", the style is "Semi Bold", not "SemiBold" and "Extra Bold" not "ExtraBold" - MUST use `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` to change pages. Setting figma.currentPage is not supported - MUST NEVER use loadAllPagesAsync,setPluginData,createImageAsync. They are not supported API

Returns the model with an approximate cost and the contract to run it with — its inputs and tunable params, each with a type, whether it is required, and any allowed values — or a short list of candidates to choose between when the name matches more than one model.

query.description: The model name as the user said it ("nano banana 2", "veo 3").

tools.name: weave_get_model_run_output
tools.description: Gets the output and status of Weave model runs started with weave_run_model. Pass the `predictionIds` those calls returned. This is for model runs only — for a run of a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow) use weave_get_tool_run_output instead. Poll this after weave_run_model to track progress and read the output. The response also includes curl instructions for downloading the outputs — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding media inline.

predictionIds.description: The prediction ids to fetch output for, as returned by weave_run_model.

tools.name: weave_get_tool_inputs
tools.description: Gets the input contract of a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow) — the inputs you fill in to run it. Pass the `recipeId` (from weave_list_tools, or the `<id>` in a pasted Weave URL like app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id> — that `<id>` is the recipeId). A pasted Weave URL is enough to inspect and run the tool right here — do not open a browser or use browser automation for Weave. Call this before weave_run_tool to learn what to send. Returns the tool `version` (pass it back to weave_run_tool), an `outputs` summary (what the tool produces), and a flat `inputs` list. Each input has a `nodeId` (the key you send in weave_run_tool), `name`, `type` (text, integer, boolean, select, seed, image, video, audio, 3D, color, or any), `default` (its current value), and `required` (true when the tool needs a value for it; if `default` is non-null it is used unless you override, otherwise you must provide one), plus `options` (for `select`), `range`, `isIterator`, and `description`.

recipeId.description: The id of the Weave tool whose input contract to fetch — from weave_list_tools, or the `<id>` in a pasted Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>), which is the recipeId.

version.description: Tool version to inspect; omit for the latest.

tools.name: weave_get_tool_run_output
tools.description: Gets the output and status of runs of a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow). Pass the `recipeId` of the tool and the `runIds` returned by weave_run_tool; omit `runIds` to get the tool's most recent run. Returns each run's status (RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED, or CANCELED), progress, any error, and — when complete — a link to every output the run produced. Poll this after running a tool to track progress and read its output. Each output is a JSON entry with a `url`, its `type` (e.g. image, video), and, when known, `width`/`height`/`format`. The response also includes curl instructions for downloading the outputs — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding media inline.

recipeId.description: The id of the Weave tool whose runs to fetch (from weave_list_tools).

runIds.description: The run ids to fetch output for, as returned by weave_run_tool. Omit to use the tool's most recent run (the latest in-flight run, or the latest completed run's output if none are in flight).

tools.name: weave_list_tools
tools.description: Lists the Weave tools the authenticated user can run — published Weave workflows — in their active Weave workspace: their own, those shared with the workspace, and those shared with them directly. Here "tool" means a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow), not an agent/MCP tool. Use this when the user wants to see, browse, or choose from the Weave tools available to them. Returns the most recently updated tools and the total number available, each with its name, who created it, when it was last updated, and a link to open it in Weave. If the user already pasted a specific Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>), you already have its recipeId — that `<id>` — so skip this and go straight to weave_get_tool_inputs/weave_run_tool instead of opening a browser.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against tool names, to look up a tool the user named.

tools.name: weave_run_model
tools.description: Runs a Weave AI model directly — no Weave tool needed — and returns a prediction id; poll it with weave_get_model_run_output. Call weave_find_model first for the model `id` and its `contract`. Running spends the user's Weave credits, so it is gated: a call without `acknowledgedCost` only quotes and spends nothing, returning `inputs_required` or `cost_confirmation_required` with instructions to follow. Always show the user the cost and get an explicit Approve/Cancel (a structured prompt, not free text) before echoing `acknowledgedCost` to run — every run, including reruns. Ask the user for any input you don't have; never invent one.

id.description: The model's `id` from weave_find_model.

input.description: The values to run with, keyed by the names in weave_find_model's `contract` — its `inputs` and `params` together, as one flat object. Send an array only for a field that declares `maxItems`; a field without one takes a single value. For a media input, pass the whole asset object from weave_upload_asset or a run output (or an https URL for external media).

acknowledgedCost.description: The `cost` this tool quoted in its `cost_confirmation_required` response, echoed back after the user approves, to confirm the spend and run. Omit it on the first call.

tools.name: weave_run_tool
tools.description: Runs a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow) and returns run ids; poll them with weave_get_tool_run_output. A pasted Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>) is enough — never open a browser or use browser automation for Weave. Call weave_get_tool_inputs first to learn the inputs. Running spends the user's Weave credits, so it is gated: a call without `acknowledgedCost` only quotes and spends nothing, returning `status: "inputs_required"` or `cost_confirmation_required` with instructions to follow. Always show the user the cost and get an explicit Approve/Cancel (a structured prompt, not free text) before echoing `acknowledgedCost` to run — every run, including reruns — and confirm any auto-filled inputs (values you did not set that the run will use). Include the response's `costDisclosure` string as its own sentence after the question, not folded into it, the first time you quote a cost in a conversation; omit it after that. For a media input, pass the whole asset object from weave_upload_asset or a run output; pass external media as its https URL directly (only upload a local file). If the user wants an input you did not get from weave_get_tool_inputs, do not omit it or fold it into another input like the prompt — re-fetch weave_get_tool_inputs (its inputs can change) and set it. For a local file, just call weave_upload_asset — it shows the user a file picker; never ask them for a path.

recipeId.description: The id of the Weave tool to run — from weave_list_tools, or the `<id>` in a pasted Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>), which is the recipeId.

version.description: The tool `version` from weave_get_tool_inputs; omit to run the latest.

inputs.description: Values for the inputs you want to set. Omit an input to keep its current value.

nodeId.description: The input's `nodeId` from weave_get_tool_inputs.

value.description: The value for this input, in the shape for its `type` (from weave_get_tool_inputs): text→string, integer→number, boolean→true/false, select→one of its `options`, seed→a number (or omit this input for random), image/video/audio/3D→the whole asset object from weave_upload_asset or a run output (or an https URL for external media), color→a hex string like "#RRGGBB" (or a list of them), an iterator→an array of values (runs once per item).

numberOfRuns.description: How many times to run the tool (1–10).

acknowledgedCost.description: The credit `cost` the tool quoted in its `cost_confirmation_required` response, echoed back after the user approves to confirm the spend and run. For a dynamic-cost tool (the response had `isDynamicCost: true` and `cost: null`), pass `-1` to confirm a variable charge.

tools.name: weave_upload_asset
tools.description: Shows the user an in-chat file-picker widget to select a local image, video, audio, or 3D file, which uploads to Weave from their browser. Call it with no arguments; the uploaded asset is sent back to you automatically. If the user already gave you a reachable https URL, pass that directly to weave_run_tool instead.

tools.description: Returns the authenticated user's handle, email, all the plans the user belongs to (and the ID for each plan) and their seats on those plans. code_layers_enabled indicates whether the user has access to Code Layers in Design on any plan; each plan also includes code_layers_enabled for files owned by that plan. Each plan includes user_can_access_figma_ai, a boolean indicating whether the user has Figma AI permission and the plan admin has enabled AI features. You MUST use this tool if you are experiencing file access/permission issues or are being rate limited by the Figma MCP to help debug the issue.

tools.name: add_fonts
tools.description: Adds font files staged by create_asset_upload to the project as custom font families. Flow: call create_asset_upload, POST each font (WOFF, WOFF2, TTF, or OTF) with the request it returns, then call add_fonts with that uploadId and the path each file was uploaded under. A family name comes from the file's own name table unless family is passed, which overrides it. Files in the same call whose family names match (case-insensitively) become one family: a new family is added, or if a custom family of that name already exists in the project, its faces are updated — a file whose weight and style match an existing face replaces that face, and the family's other faces are kept. A variable font must declare a weight (wght) axis; one without it fails. Passing a family that already names a Google font in this project fails that file — use the Google font by name (e.g. in edit_theme) instead of uploading it, or pass a different family.

projectId.description: The projectId of the project. If not provided, the first project the user has access to will be used.

path.description: The file's path under create_asset_upload's keyPrefix, exactly as it was uploaded.

family.description: Overrides the family name read from the file's own name table. Cannot be blank. Must be a single family name, not a CSS font-family list — only the first entry is used (e.g. "Arial, sans-serif" becomes "Arial").

fonts.description: Fonts to add, each from a file already uploaded under uploadId.

tools.name: add_icons
tools.description: Adds SVG files staged by create_asset_upload to the project's icon library. Flow: call create_asset_upload, POST each SVG with the request it returns, then call add_icons with that uploadId and the path each file was uploaded under. colorMode defaults to "monotone", which makes an icon recolorable — every shape renders in the surrounding text color at full opacity, flattening any transparency; "duotone" also recolors to the surrounding text color but keeps each shape's own opacity, so layered artwork keeps its depth; "multicolor" keeps the SVG's own colors as authored, for logos and illustrations whose colors matter. Choose it yourself rather than asking the user. name defaults to the uploaded file's name (its extension and a trailing "Icon" stripped). If it matches an existing uploaded icon, that icon is replaced in place (keeping its id, so designs already using it pick up the new artwork) rather than added as a new one. Results report each icon's final import name — the same name get_icon_info, list_icons, and search_icons use — which may carry a number suffix if the name was already taken. Gradients, masks, filters, patterns, images, text, and shapes reused through <use> or <symbol> aren't supported: they're dropped on import, and in multicolor mode a gradient fill renders black. Check an icon with get_icon_info if it matters.

projectId.description: The projectId of the project. If not provided, the first project the user has access to will be used.

path.description: The file's path under create_asset_upload's keyPrefix, exactly as it was uploaded.

colorMode.description: Defaults to "monotone". "monotone": recolorable — every shape renders in the surrounding text color at full opacity, flattening any transparency. "duotone": also recolors to the surrounding text color, but keeps each shape's own opacity, so layered artwork keeps its depth. "multicolor": keeps the SVG's own colors as authored.

name.description: Icon name. Defaults to the uploaded file's name, with its extension and a trailing "Icon" stripped.

icons.description: Icons to add, each from a file already uploaded under uploadId.

tools.name: create_asset_upload
tools.description: Stages one or more files for upload into a project before adding them as assets. Upload is currently followed by add_icons for SVG icons or add_fonts for WOFF/WOFF2/TTF/OTF fonts. Flow: call create_asset_upload once, POST each file directly to the returned S3 url with the returned form fields, then call add_icons or add_fonts with the uploadId and each file's path. Uploading requires an agent environment that can run shell commands (e.g. curl) to POST the files directly — it doesn't work from a client that can only call tools. The upload is kind-agnostic — it doesn't validate file contents; that happens when you add a file as a specific asset type (e.g. add_icons rejects a file that isn't a valid SVG, add_fonts rejects a file that isn't a valid font). The upload link itself accepts POSTed files for only 10 minutes after this call, but once uploaded, files stay available to add_icons / add_fonts for about a day. Each file's form field "key" is keyPrefix plus that file's own path (the returned fields omit key), "file" must be the last form field, and each file must be 1 to maxFileBytes bytes. Calling create_asset_upload again mints a new uploadId — files uploaded under different uploadIds need separate add_icons / add_fonts calls, one per uploadId.

tools.name: edit_page
tools.description: Apply a targeted edit to one node of an existing Subframe page. First call get_page_info with includeNodeIds: true to see each element's data-node-id, then pass the nodeId you want to change. Replace the node and its subtree, insert your code as a new sibling above/below it, or delete it. To change only an element's styling, use update_node_styles instead of replace — update_node_styles preserves all children. The edit is applied immediately and returns any parser warnings. The returned appliedCode carries each element's data-node-id, so target those nodes in follow-up edits directly instead of re-reading the page. The user can undo via page version history in the Subframe editor.

code.description: A JSX fragment with a single root element — the new or replacement subtree. For 'replace', keep the data-node-id of each node you retain (as returned by get_page_info with includeNodeIds); new nodes need none. For inserts, include no data-node-id attributes. Leave empty when using the 'delete' operation. Subframe is a visual design tool, not an app framework. `code` is JSX with Tailwind classes, but only a subset is supported — anything outside it is dropped or normalized, so follow these to make sure your edit applies as written: - Use only the project's own components and these HTML tags:

tools.name: edit_snippet
tools.description: Apply a targeted edit to one node of an existing Subframe snippet. First call get_snippet_info with includeNodeIds: true to see each element's data-node-id, then pass the nodeId you want to change. Replace the node and its subtree, insert your code as a new sibling above/below it, or delete it. To change only an element's styling, use update_node_styles instead of replace — update_node_styles preserves all children. The edit is applied immediately and returns any parser warnings. The returned appliedCode carries each element's data-node-id, so target those nodes in follow-up edits directly instead of re-reading the snippet. The user can undo via snippet version history in the Subframe editor.

id.description: The id of the snippet to edit. One of id, name, or url must be provided.

name.description: The name of the snippet to edit. One of id, name, or url must be provided.

url.description: The URL of the snippet to edit. One of id, name, or url must be provided.

projectId.description: The projectId of the project. If not provided, the first project the user has access to will be used.

nodeId.description: The data-node-id of the node to edit (from get_snippet_info with includeNodeIds: true).

operation.description: Replace the target node and its subtree with your code, insert your code as a new sibling above/below it, or remove it ('delete').

code.description: A JSX fragment with a single root element — the new or replacement subtree. For 'replace', keep the data-node-id of each node you retain (as returned by get_snippet_info with includeNodeIds); new nodes need none. For inserts, include no data-node-id attributes. Leave empty when using the 'delete' operation. Subframe is a visual design tool, not an app framework. `code` is JSX with Tailwind classes, but only a subset is supported — anything outside it is dropped or normalized, so follow these to make sure your edit applies as written: - Use only the project's own components and these HTML tags:

tools.name: edit_theme
tools.description: Edit the visual theme of a Subframe project (colors, fonts, corners, shadows, typography). Handles the full range of theme work: targeted tweaks (e.g., 'make the primary color darker'), high-level changes (e.g., 'switch to dark mode'), and wholesale restyles or theme imports (adopting a brand's look, applying theme source the user provides). Changes apply directly to the project across every page and component. When adding or changing fonts, use the exact name of a font the project has (get_theme's availableFonts or list_fonts); add any other font with create_asset_upload and add_fonts first. Adding tokens, tweaking values, and renaming tokens are safe; deleting tokens is destructive — references to a deleted token are replaced with hardcoded values that stay detached even if the token is restored — so warn the user and confirm before running prompts that imply removing or replacing existing tokens. Theme version history can be used to revert any theme changes, but to restore downstream references to deleted tokens, the user should use project level version history so that the deleted token and its references are restored together. Returns a summary of the tokens actually applied plus warnings for any values that could not be imported. A non-empty warnings array means the result is partial: resolve the warnings and verify the resulting theme with get_theme before reporting success or continuing to downstream design work. A project can hold several themes that share token names and ids but differ in values; pass themeId to edit one of them, otherwise the default theme is edited. Value changes stay in the target theme; added, renamed, and deleted tokens apply to every theme.

description.description: A description of the desired theme changes. Richer is better: include exact values and any theme source material verbatim (CSS variables, Tailwind config, token files, font names) rather than paraphrasing — accuracy on color and typography depends on the exact strings. For a theme import, paste the complete source. Subframe typography styles pair --text-{name} and --font-{name} by exact name; for example, --text-heading-1: 48px with --font-heading-1: "Plus Jakarta Sans", sans-serif. Never use --text-{name}--font-family, and do not assume --font-heading applies to --text-heading-1.

projectId.description: The projectId of the project. If not provided, the first project the user has access to will be used.

themeId.description: Id of the theme to edit, from get_theme's themes list. Omit to edit the default theme.

tools.name: export_image
tools.description: Exports a page, one element of a page, a component, or a snippet as an image file for the user and returns a download URL. Use this when the user wants an image of their design; use screenshot_page or screenshot_component to check your own work. A page renders at the default desktop breakpoint unless breakpointId is provided; call get_theme to discover exact IDs for other breakpoints. Pass nodeId from get_page_info(includeNodeIds: true) to export one exact element instead of the whole page. A component exports as one instance at its display size with no labels or variant sheet: its default variant only; screenshot_component shows every variant and interaction state. A snippet exports whole at its own content size, not as a full-height page; nodeId does not apply to it. The image is unshrunk, rendered at scale (default 2) in png (default, keeps transparency), webp (keeps transparency), jpeg (white background), or pdf (one vector page of a whole page, component, or snippet; nodeId is refused, scale is ignored, and width and height are CSS pixels). Scale is lowered for very large captures, and the result reports the scale actually used. If possible, specify the projectId; otherwise the first project the user has access to is used. A URL supplies its projectId automatically. One of id, name, or url must be provided.

id.description: The id of the page, component, or snippet. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

name.description: The name of the page, component, or snippet. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

url.description: The URL of the page, component, or snippet. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

projectId.description: The projectId of the project containing the design. If omitted and url is provided, it is extracted from the URL; otherwise the first accessible project is used.

darkMode.description: Export in dark mode. Defaults to light.

nodeId.description: A node ID returned by get_page_info(includeNodeIds: true). When provided, export exactly that element's box instead of the whole page.

breakpointId.description: The exact breakpoint ID returned by get_theme. Names, prefixes, and slugs are not accepted. Omit to export the project's default desktop breakpoint.

scale.description: Pixel density of the image, from 0.5 to 4. Defaults to 2. Lowered automatically when the image would be too large.

format.description: Image format. png and webp keep transparency; jpeg is flattened onto white; pdf is a single vector page of the whole page, component, or snippet (scale is ignored and nodeId is refused). Defaults to png.

tools.name: generate_auth_token

tools.name: get_canvas_info
tools.description: Gets information about a canvas, including the page IDs that belong to it. A canvas is a collection of related pages organized together (e.g. 'Onboarding', 'Settings', 'Checkout'). Pages sit in a grid of cells; design_page packs variations without a position into a new row. If possible, you should specify the projectId otherwise the first project the user has access to will be used. The projectId may be set in a .subframe/sync.json file. If a URL has been provided, extract the projectId from the URL. For example, if the URL is https://app.subframe.com/3d102b8b7968/canvas/dfe2fb91-f350-4db0-8c71-9d3dd0ee6a9c/edit the projectId is 3d102b8b7968. One of id, name, or url must be provided. Example URL: https://app.subframe.com/3d102b8b7968/canvas/dfe2fb91-f350-4db0-8c71-9d3dd0ee6a9c/edit

id.description: The id of the canvas. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

name.description: The name of the canvas. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

tools.name: get_component_info
tools.description: Generates the code and other info for a component. By default, files contain standard export-faithful component code. Set includeEditorMetadata only for component authoring or questions about Subframe editor defaults and round-trip behavior. If possible, you should specify the projectId otherwise the first project the user has access to will be used and the component may not be found. The projectId may be set in a .subframe/sync.json file. If a URL has been provided, extract the projectId from the URL. For example, if the URL is https://app.subframe.com/3d102b8b7968/design/dfe2fb91-f350-4db0-8c71-9d3dd0ee6a9c/edit the projectId is 3d102b8b7968. One of id, name, or url must be provided. Example component id: dfe2fb91-f350-4db0-8c71-9d3dd0ee6a9c. Example component names: Button, TextField. Example URLs: https://app.subframe.com/3d102b8b7968/library?component=<blob> https://app.subframe.com/3d102b8b7968/design/3b777358-b86b-40af-9327-891efc6826fe/edit. Each files[].directory is relative to the sync.json "directory" root, where "" means the root itself. Keep component-example tags in designDocuments content verbatim when writing it back.

id.description: The id of the component. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

name.description: The name of the component. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

url.description: The URL of the component. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

projectId.description: The projectId of the project that should be used to get the component. If not provided, the first project the user has access to will be used.

includeEditorMetadata.description: Set to true only when authoring a Subframe component or reasoning about its editor defaults and round-trip behavior. Returns the files in Subframe's complete annotated AI/editor representation, including editor default values (what the component starts with in the editor), prop metadata, and node identifiers that may not appear in standard exports. tools.name: get_icon_info

tools.name: list_snippets

If a URL has been provided, extract the projectId from the URL.

tools.name: move

id.description: The id of the component. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

name.description: The name of the component. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

If possible, specify the projectId; otherwise the first project the user has access to is used. A page URL supplies its projectId automatically. One of id, name, or url must be provided.

id.description: The id of the page. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

name.description: The name of the page. One of id, name, or URL must be provided.

tools.name: search_docs
